nodes.question: Compare the source and edited images. Identify the source mug and headphones, then determine whether the same mug has moved relative to the headphones and where it ends up. If multiple mugs or visual artifacts make the source mug's identity or movement unclear, report unknown rather than treating another mug as the requested mug.
nodes.criteria: Complete only when the source mug is identifiable in the edited image and has been moved to the right of the headphones. Partial when the same mug has moved toward the right but remains not to their right. Absent when the same mug shows no movement toward the right. Unknown when the source mug's identity, movement, or relative position cannot be established from the images. Do not count a different or newly appearing mug as progress.
nodes.binding: The mug in the source image (a blue mug to the left of the headphones) and the headphones; assess the source mug's movement and final position in the edited image.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.
